description: 8 retrieval probes for sinatra/sinatra — an MIT-licensed Ruby web DSL with module helpers, class << self singleton methods, Rack-class inheritance, and Struct.new subclassing.

probes.query: how does sinatra match incoming requests to route handlers and dispatch the response
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: Sinatra::Base (line 971) is the core class that owns the route table and dispatch logic

probes.query: how does sinatra extend Rack Request with HTTP content negotiation methods like accept
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: Sinatra::Request (line 31) extends Rack::Request and adds accept / preferred_type / accept? — the Content-Type negotiation surface

probes.query: how does sinatra cache compiled view templates between requests
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: Sinatra::TemplateCache (line 949) memoizes compiled templates keyed by path+engine

probes.query: Sinatra Application class extending Base for the top-level DSL
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: Sinatra::Application < Base (line 2085) backs the top-level get/post/etc. DSL

probes.query: Sinatra IndifferentHash class for string and symbol key access
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: IndifferentHash provides symbol-or-string key normalization — its own file

probes.query: Sinatra Helpers module mixed into Base
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: Sinatra::Helpers (line 286) is the module of view/response helpers included into request handlers

probes.query: Sinatra Base class << self block for class-level DSL definitions
probes.notes: Grammar-edge-case probe: Sinatra::Base has multiple `class << self ... end` blocks (lines 1290, 1965) that open the singleton class to define class-level DSL methods (get/post/etc.). Exercises tree-sitter-ruby's handling of singleton_class — the chunker must attribute these to Base, not emit them as orphaned chunks

probes.query: ExtendedRack class inheriting from a Struct.new runtime-generated class
probes.notes: Grammar-edge-case probe: `class ExtendedRack < Struct.new(:app)` (line 225) is a Ruby idiom where the superclass expression is a method call returning a runtime-generated Struct class. Exercises tree-sitter-ruby's handling of class declarations whose superclass slot is a call_expression, not a constant reference
